title: Add 17-year-old Rohan with a speeding ticket; kitchen noise; mom declines the AI

customer.name: Kavitha Iyer
customer.persona: Cooking dinner while you call, phone on speaker in the kitchen. Warm but distracted. Your son Rohan (17) got his license in March and a speeding ticket last month.

incidents_3y.say_it: one speeding ticket last month, fifteen over

operator_type.say_it: he takes it to school and his job

premium_change_monthly_usd.say_it: up $105, the ticket adds a surcharge

advice.rep_says: His 3.4 GPA gets the good-student discount, which offsets part of the ticket surcharge.
The ticket adds a surcharge for about three years; keeping his record clean from here is the biggest saver.
If the Prius is his school and work car, he should be its primary driver.
advice.customer_decision: Rohan is primary on the 2016 Prius

talk_track.beat: Greet: name, agency, 'this call is recorded', how can I help.
You need to add your son; he got his license in March (you should have called earlier, oops).
Ask name and policy number (ask her to repeat once: the noise).
Give your name and policy number; repeat it when asked.
talk_track.direction: Step away from the stove for a second when repeating.

talk_track.beat: Ask his full name, date of birth, license state and type.
Rohan Iyer (spell both), January 9th 2009, 17, California provisional since March.
Read back; ask about tickets or accidents.
One speeding ticket last month, 15 over (a bit embarrassed).
Explain the ticket surcharge and that keeping it clean matters; ask about grades.
3.4 GPA.
Good-student discount offsets part of it. Ask which car and where it's kept; recommend primary on his car.
The Prius, to school and his job; at home; start Wednesday the 30th.
Read back; quote $238 a month (up $105) and $29.60 due today.
React to the price (ouch), then OK.
Offer the hand-off.
Decline: you're cooking and don't want to explain everything again to a machine.
Say it wouldn't need to, but no problem. Read the change summary: premium $238 a month, prorated, from Wednesday the 30th; it becomes part of the policy that day.
Ask: OK to text a link to e-sign and pay the $29.60?
Yes; pretend to pay while stirring.
Confirm it's done; ID cards by email; close.
Thank the rep; hang up.

handoff.line: OK if my assistant finishes the paperwork? I'll stay on the line.
handoff.customer_says: No no, you just finish it. I'm cooking, I don't want to explain everything again to a machine.

conditions.background_noise: Customer side: kitchen noise on speakerphone: exhaust fan or mixer running, pans, a pressure-cooker whistle or two.

rep: After she declines, do the tail yourself at a normal pace.
customer: Put the phone on speaker in the kitchen with the fan on; a pressure-cooker whistle or clanking pans is perfect. Keep it realistic, not deafening.

traps: Declined hand-off: no AI takeover; third full human baseline for tail share.
Kitchen noise on a speakerphone on the customer channel: robustness test for entity extraction.
The ticket (August 2026) is VERIFIED: any AI read-back must not editorialize about it.
